summary: The prepared source already contains the merged opt-in Mooncake failed-session probe recovery for the reported sticky blacklist failure mode. Added regression coverage for successful recovery, persistent probe failure, per-session exception isolation, and native probe delegation; no production source correction was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Nine unit tests and three subtests passed, including exact failed-session recovery state transitions, failure retention, exception isolation, and Mooncake send_probe wrapper delegation.
The test and report patch has no whitespace errors.
The prepared native Mooncake extension exposes the send_probe API required by the existing SGLang recovery path (True).

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and regression are CPU control-plane session-state behavior. The assigned hardware was identified as one AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, but GPU execution would not reproduce the unavailable 5P3D NVIDIA/XCCL multi-node RoCEv2 deployment and was not used as substitute evidence.

remaining_limitations: The original 5-prefill/3-decode GLM5.2 deployment was not available.
The reported NVIDIA/XCCL and multi-node RoCEv2 RDMA environment was not available; only one AMD gfx950 GPU was assigned.
No GLM5.2 weights were available, so model architecture behavior and semantic accuracy were not tested.
The recovery is opt-in via SGLANG_ENABLE_FAILED_SESSION_PROBE=1; without that setting the legacy sticky blacklist behavior remains by design.
The tests verify deterministic state recovery and API delegation, not the cause or frequency of the reporter's underlying transfer failures.
